history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Meerut' is wrong - the temple is in Modi Nagar (Modinagar), Ghaziabad district, roughly 35-40 km southwest of Meerut; town and district corrected. The famous Laxmi Narayan Mandir at Modinagar, popularly known as 'Modi Mandir', was built in 1963 by Rai Bahadur Gujar Mal (G.M.) Modi and his wife Mrs. Dayawati Modi; it is one of the temples managed by the Modi foundation and draws devotees from far and near. The Mandir complex has a large open-air theatre where the annual Ramleela is enacted, and hosts daily prayers and lectures by spiritual leaders. Note: G.M. Modi (founder of the Modi Group and of the industrial city of Modinagar in 1933) was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1968. A Meerut travel portal confirms the temple occupies more than 15 acres.

name: Lakshmi Narayan Mandir
town_description: Modi Nagar (Modinagar) is an industrial city in Ghaziabad district, western Uttar Pradesh, founded in 1933 by Rai Bahadur Gujar Mal Modi around his sugar mill; it anchors the Modi Group's industrial township on the Delhi-Meerut corridor (NH-58), with schools, hospitals and cultural institutions built by the founding family.
